claims.statement: The ECS cluster routes ECS Exec transcripts to a dedicated encrypted CloudWatch log group; the main container and optional kube-proxy sidecar write to a separate group with distinct stream prefixes.
The three functions have separate retention-controlled log groups. Task reaper logs distinguish stops from deferrals.

On normal process exit and trapped SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP alike, entrypoint.sh's cleanup() runs sync_to_s3 under a nested watchdog: it requires both a 32-hex-character ECS task ID (from task metadata) and a pattern-matching INVESTIGATION_ID before writing anything, otherwise it aborts with an 'unverified'/'missing_correlation' warning; a successful attempt writes workspace files plus a report.json under a fresh per-attempt UUID path, always marked status:"unverified"; the sync excludes '.config/ocm/*' and '.kube/*' and does not follow symlinks; and any missing configuration, failed transfer, or timeout produces a warning rather than guaranteeing persistence or blocking the container from exiting.

The investigation audit bucket is versioned and uses compliance-mode Object Lock, blocks public access, applies AES-256 encryption, denies non-TLS requests, and can replicate cross-account. The task IAM role is granted PutObject and ListBucket but is explicitly denied PutObject on the operator's '_boundary-close/*' close-receipt prefix and on the reaper's '*/*/reaper-final-backup/*' prefix; docs/configuration/aws-iam-policies.md states that the SRE exec grant is not an audit-reader grant and that CloudWatch/S3 reads require a separately authorized operator/audit-reader identity, whose concrete role and access procedure are defined in the audit-log-access runbook's 'rosa-boundary-audit-reader' role rather than in that doc itself.

Bedrock invocation logging is configured for text payloads across Bedrock Runtime callers in the account and Region, sending payloads up to 100 KB to encrypted CloudWatch Logs and larger payloads to a separate S3 bucket; image, embedding and video delivery are disabled.

The shell tests verify that both explicit S3_AUDIT_ESCROW and bucket/cluster/investigation/task-generated destinations produce a fresh per-attempt UUID and a correlated report.json (schema_version, investigation_id, task_id, transfer_rc, status always "unverified"), and that a missing investigation ID, ECS metadata URI, explicit escrow, or task ARN aborts sync_to_s3 before any aws s3 sync call with a logged result=unverified reason. The LocalStack integration tests separately verify that nested OCM and kubeconfig files are excluded from the S3 sync while unrelated workspace files remain eligible, using token/account-response canaries.
The investigation sweep logs discovery errors and summary counts. Logs help diagnose retries; they do not establish successful verification.
The finalizer copies the workspace and verifies its contents before cleanup. A service-issued receipt identifies the verified attempt and records cleanup separately.
Terraform sets INVESTIGATION_EXPIRY_HOURS from investigation_grace_period_hours; both defaults are 168 hours.
Sweep eligibility distinguishes idle from expired investigations. Missing CreatedAt means expired; an invalid timestamp is logged as an error.

Staging declares east and west regional workspaces; their log-group names can match because the names omit Region, whereas the audit bucket naming rule includes account and Region, so retrieval must select the account and Region explicitly.

The audit-access runbook directs users to request a separately managed rosa-boundary-audit-reader S3 role through app-interface and authenticate through SAML without --assume-uid; it explicitly requires separate CloudWatch Logs read permissions. The account-baseline guide states that this Terraform baseline does not add an audit-reader role.

The shared Bedrock logging role restricts service assumption to the source account and explicitly approved source-region ARN patterns, with staging listing us-east-1 and us-west-2; invocation-logging configurations, destinations and inline delivery grants remain regional rather than combining logs through the shared role.

deploy/regional/variables.tf defaults log_retention_days to seven days while Git-managed HCP configuration overrides this to 90 for both staging and both production regional workspaces. CloudWatch container and Lambda log groups consume this setting, so they retain 90 days wherever the workspace values have actually been applied.

The HCP Terraform map declares a production account workspace allowing Bedrock log sources in east and west, with corresponding network and regional workspaces in both Regions; the account and both network and regional workspaces declare remote execution and auto-apply, while prod AWS credentials require manual apply. The configuration alone does not prove latest run status or that audit logs are live.
TA emits its own structured audit records routed via CloudWatch and Firehose to its audit bucket, separate from Boundary transcripts and workspace evidence.
TaskCreationRequests measures outcomes by ECS cluster. The optional ActorUUID is a log property, not a metric dimension or proof of investigation closure.

On both the trapped-signal path and the normal-exit path, entrypoint.sh routes into the same cleanup() function, which first sends SIGTERM to the workload child process and to the optional background skill reconciler (stop_skill_reconciler) without itself waiting; the watchdog-wrapped subshell that follows then runs await_writers, which polls for up to ~3 seconds until both the workload child PID and the reconciler PID have exited, before sync_to_s3 executes. This ordering improves the shutdown sync's point-in-time fidelity by stopping the one process most likely to still be writing into /home/sre; it does not make the sync transactional, since other ECS Exec sessions or tasks sharing the EFS directory are not fenced.
